raw_segments.text: In such conversation an hour was soon gone. Bessie restored to me my bonnet, and sea,
and accompanied by her, I quitted the lodge for the hall. It was also accompanied by her
that I had, nearly nine years ago, walked down the path I was now ascending. On a dark,
misty, raw morning in January, I had left a hostile roof with a desperate and embittered
heart, a sense of outlawry and almost of reprobation, to seek the chilly harborage of loade, that
borne so far away and unexplored. The same hostile roof now again rose before me,
my prospects were doubtful yet, and I had yet an aching heart. I still felt as a wanderer on
the face of the earth, but I experienced firmer trust in myself and my own powers,
and less withering dread of oppression. The gaping wound of my wrongs, too,
was now quite healed, and the flame of resentment extinguished.
